results.evidence: InviteRow computes `isExistingMember = existingMemberEmails.has(targetEmail.trim().toLowerCase())`, adds ' errored' class and renders 'This person is already a member of your organization.' inline. InviteRow is shared by the settings dialog.
existingMemberEmails selector pushes `user.email` into the set, so own email is flagged the same way.

canSubmit is false with existing members, but the batch submit control's reason/tooltip is not shown anywhere in the patch (no 'remove people who are already members' message). Per-row Submit is disabled only in the no-email-service layout; with email service there is no per-row send control change. The required communicated reason is missing.
Both set construction and lookups use `.trim().toLowerCase()`.
`afterMount(({ actions }) => { actions.ensureAllMembersLoaded() })` and the selector handles `members ?? []` while still adding user.email, so own-email check works before load.

The check moved into `validate_target_email`, which runs during serializer validation (bulk with many=True validates all rows before create), so no invites are created for the batch. The bulk view code isn't shown, but this is standard DRF behavior.

`raise exceptions.ValidationError("A user with this email address already belongs to the organization.")` has no code. It is field-level via validate_target_email, but lacks a stable distinguishable code (compare the `code="verified_domain_required"` used nearby).
No frontend or backend change to suppress error tracking. The author admits they did not trace the error-tracking path.
No handler on inviteTeamMembersFailure to refresh members when the server rejects an existing member; listeners only handle success.

result:
Inviting an existing member (or yourself) is now flagged on the invite row before you submit, and a batch containing one is rejected up front. I haven't run any tests, typechecks or the app.

**Backend (`posthog/api/organization_invite.py`)**
- The "already belongs to the organization" check used to run inside `create()`. In a bulk request the earlier rows had already been created and emailed by then.
- I moved it into `validate_target_email`, so it runs with the rest of the validation before anything is saved. A bulk batch with an existing member in any row now fails with a 400, and no invites are created or emailed.
- Because it's now an ordinary validation error, it should no longer be reported to error tracking as an unexpected error. I didn't trace the error-tracking path itself, so that's the expectation, not something I confirmed.
- I added `test_bulk_invite_with_existing_member_creates_no_invites` in `posthog/api/test/test_organization_invites.py`. It sends two valid rows plus the requester's own email, then asserts a 400, zero invites and no `send_invite` call.

**Frontend**
- `inviteLogic.ts` now loads the organization's members and builds an `existingMemberEmails` set. It is lowercased and includes your own email.
- `canSubmit` is false while any row's email is in that set.
- `InviteModal.tsx` shows the errored input style and a message under the email field ("This person is already a member of your organization."). In the no-email-service layout, the row's Submit button is also disabled.
- The onboarding step and the organization settings dialog share `InviteRow` and `inviteLogic`, so this covers both.
- The client-side check only sees members that `membersLogic` has loaded, so the server check is the final guard.
- I hand-edited the inline typegen block in `inviteLogic.ts`, so `typegen:file` may want to reconcile it.

The new copy is plain and follows the repo's sentence-case style. I didn't invoke the copy or test-writing skills.
